s: A company wants to use an Amazon S3 bucket for its data scientists to store documents. The company uses AWS IAM Identity Center to authenticate users. The company created an IAM Identity Center group for the data scientists. The company wants to grant the data scientists access to only their specific folders in the S3 bucket. The company also wants to know which documents each data scientist accessed. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)
o: Create a custom IAM Identity Center permission set to grant the data scientists access to an S3 bucket prefix that matches their username tag. Use a policy to limit access to paths with the ${aws:PrincipalTag/userName>/" condition.
Create an IAM Identity Center role for the data scientist group that has Amazon S3 read access and write access. Add an S3 bucket policy that allows access to the IAM Identity Center role.
Configure AWS CloudTrail to log S3 data events and deliver the logs to an S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to run queries on the CloudTrail logs in Amazon S3.
Configure AWS CloudTrail to log S3 management events to Amazon CloudWatch. Use the Amazon Athena CloudWatch connector to query the logs.
Enable S3 access logging to the EMR File System (EMRFS). Create an AWS Glue job to run queries on the access log data in EMRFS.

w.y: IAM Identity Center attributes for access control pass user attributes as session tags. One permission set can then use ${aws:PrincipalTag/userName} to limit each data scientist to their own S3 prefix (ABAC). Object-level access (GetObject/PutObject) appears only in CloudTrail S3 data events. Delivered to S3, those logs can be queried with Athena to see who accessed which documents.

o.A: Correct: an ABAC permission set with aws:PrincipalTag scopes each user to their own prefix.
o.B: One role with read/write to the whole bucket gives every data scientist access to every folder.
o.C: Correct: CloudTrail S3 data events record object-level reads; Athena queries them in S3.
o.D: Management events cover bucket-level API calls, not object reads, so document access would not be logged.
o.E: S3 server access logs cannot be delivered to EMRFS, and Glue jobs are not a query tool for this.

s: Create permission policies for ABAC in IAM Identity Center
Enabling CloudTrail event logging for S3 buckets and objects
Query AWS CloudTrail logs - Amazon Athena
